transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been feeling constantly depressed, sad, and just completely empty inside. It's not something new, either—I've felt this way for about two years and three months now, and it just doesn't seem to lift.
Have you had any periods lasting at least two months where you felt noticeably better, even if not fully happy?
No, I don't think I've had any periods of feeling noticeably better that lasted that long. I can't really recall any breaks from this low mood over the last two years; it has just been constant.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder"], but based on this conversation, Major Depressive Disorder is less likely because the patient reports a chronic, unremitting low mood for over two years without any significant periods of improvement. This duration and continuity of symptoms align more closely with Persistent Depressive Disorder (formerly known as dysthymia), which requires a depressed mood lasting at least two years in adults with no more than two months of symptom-free periods. Since the patient explicitly denies any such break, Major Depressive Disorder (which typically involves episodic major depressive episodes) becomes less likely as a sole diagnosis. Therefore, the current candidate is narrowed to Persistent Depressive Disorder.
